label: Bible Study
prompt: He shall cover thee with his _____, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
verse: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
note: God as a mother bird — feathers for cover, truth for armor.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his _____: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
verse: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
note: Job's story ends better than it began — the latter end blessed more than the beginning.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he _____, and must be awaked.
verse: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
note: Elijah's taunt on Mount Carmel: shout louder — maybe Baal is busy, travelling, or 'peradventure he sleepeth.'

label: Deep Water
prompt: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is _____.
verse: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
note: After contrasting the veil over Moses' face, Paul lands here: where the Spirit is, the veil comes off.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of _____: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
verse: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
note: Jesus' prelude to the parable of the rich fool: a man's life 'consisteth not' in the abundance of his possessions.
